minutes.headline: ZBA granted gas-station sign relief with conditions, continued a solar setback case, and extended a permit a year.
minutes.summary: The board heard a ground-mounted solar special permit at 63 Pratt Street with a 25-foot setback and large array height; it asked for more dimensions and drawings and continued it to Oct 2020 (as heard). It then heard sign relief for a new Gulf station at 400 Electric Avenue and granted it with conditions on pylon height and size and the canopy signs. A one-year extension for a lot at 41 Country Road was also granted.

decisions.decision: Solar hearing for 63 Pratt Street continued to October 2020 at 7 o'clock (as heard); applicant to supply array height drawings, leach field location from the Board of Health, and buffer options.
Sign applicant agreed to conditions that the Gulf pylon be no taller than the Mobil sign and no greater in square footage.
One-year extension for the 41 Country Road lot granted; board noted a third request would be scrutinized.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted sign relief for a new Gulf station at 400 Electric Avenue, with the pylon sign capped at the size and height of the Mobil sign on Lunenburg Shirley Road.
The same vote allowed the canopy signs as proposed, two on the front and one on the north side.
The board continued the 63 Pratt Street ground-mounted solar hearing to October 2020 (as heard), and asked for array height drawings, the leach field location and buffer options.
The board granted a one-year extension for the 41 Country Road lot and noted that a third request would be scrutinized.

why_it_matters: The sign decision sets how large and tall a new gas-station sign on Electric Avenue can be, and it ties that sign to an existing nearby one.
The solar case stays open, so the setback and buffer rules for a ground-mounted array next to neighbors on Pratt Street are not settled.
